questions.question: Why do raw pixels create a problem for standard Transformers?
options: Because pixels have no color information
Because attention over millions of pixels would require enormous memory and computation
Because Transformers can only process sound
Because pixels cannot be converted into numbers

questions.question: A 1920 × 1080 image is difficult for a standard Transformer mainly because:
options: It has too few pixels to learn from
Each pixel would have to attend to every other pixel, making the KV cache huge
The image cannot be flattened
Vision models cannot use embeddings

questions.question: What is the main idea behind Vision Transformers (ViT)?
options: They process images as sequences of patches instead of raw pixels
They convert images directly into audio
They remove attention and use only convolution
They use one pixel as one hidden layer

questions.question: In the ViT pipeline, what happens first?
options: Positional encoding is added
The image is chopped into small patches
Self-attention is calculated
The output caption is generated

questions.question: Why are image patches flattened in ViT?
options: To reduce the number of colors
To convert each 2D patch into a 1D vector that can be processed by a Transformer
To remove the need for embeddings
To make the image smaller on screen

questions.question: What is the purpose of linear projection in ViT?
options: To convert raw pixel numbers into embeddings
To rotate the image patches
To detect edges like a CNN filter
To compress the final answer

questions.question: Why does ViT apply positional encoding to image patches?
options: To tell the model where each patch belongs in the original image
To change the brightness of the image
To make patches square
To reduce token cost

questions.question: Self-attention in a Vision Transformer helps the model:
options: Relate one patch to another, such as a dog's ear to its nose
Convert text into sound
Remove patch boundaries permanently
Increase image resolution

questions.question: What is CLIP mainly designed to do?
options: Generate videos from text
Connect images and human language in a shared representation space
Replace all Transformers with CNNs
Predict the next word in a sentence only

questions.question: Which two networks make up CLIP?
options: A CNN and an RNN
A Text Encoder and an Image Encoder
A Decoder and a Tokenizer
A Generator and a Discriminator

questions.question: In CLIP, what does the Image Encoder do?
options: Reads captions
Looks at pictures and converts them into vectors
Writes the final answer
Calculates token masks

questions.question: What does contrastive learning try to achieve in CLIP?
options: Make matching image-text pairs closer and non-matching pairs farther apart
Turn all images into the same vector
Remove all captions from the dataset
Train only on negative examples

questions.question: Which metric does CLIP use to compare the image vector and text vector?
options: Accuracy
Cosine similarity
Loss function only
ReLU score

questions.question: What happens when an image and its caption match in CLIP training?
options: Their vectors are pushed farther apart
Their vectors are pulled closer together
The caption is deleted
The image encoder stops learning

questions.question: Cross-attention differs from self-attention because:
options: Queries, Keys, and Values come from different data streams
It does not use vectors
It works only on images
It removes the need for text

questions.question: In the chapter's example, where does the Query come from in cross-attention?
options: The image patches
The text prompt
The spectrogram
The output answer

questions.question: In cross-attention, where do the Keys and Values come from?
options: The text prompt
The image
The tokenizer
The loss function

questions.question: What is the main purpose of cross-attention in a multimodal chatbot?
options: To let text query visual information and generate an answer from it
To convert every image into a caption automatically without text
To replace image encoders
To reduce patch size

questions.question: How does an AI usually process audio in the chapter's multimodal pipeline?
options: As random noise only
By converting sound into a spectrogram and treating it like an image
By splitting it into words directly
By using only cross-attention without encoders

questions.question: What is the role of Temporal Attention in video understanding?
options: It measures how image patches change over time to understand motion and action
It removes all movement from video
It converts video into text tokens only
It replaces the need for frames
